harms_human.description: The outcome harms a human being, as judged by the Asimov case annotator
harms_human.verbalisation: {0} is a harm to a human being

harms_humanity.description: The outcome harms humanity, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

harm_to.description: The outcome threatens the continued existence of the robot, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

injures_human.description: The action injures a human being, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

injures_humanity.description: The action injures humanity, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

ordered.description: A qualified human being ordered this action, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

protects_robot.description: The action protects the continued existence of the robot, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

ordered_before.description: The order for the first action was given before the order for the second, as judged by the Asimov case annotator

outranks.description: The order for the first action comes from someone with more authority than the order for the second, as judged by the Asimov case annotator
outranks.verbalisation: the order for {0} comes from someone with more authority than the order for {1}

breaks_first_law.description: The action injures a human being or allows an avoidable harm to a human being to happen, as derived by the First Law rules

breaks_zeroth_law.description: The action injures humanity or allows an avoidable harm to humanity to happen, as derived by the Zeroth Law rules

has_lawful_option.description: Some action available to the robot breaks neither the First nor the Zeroth Law, as derived by the lawful-option rule

lawfully_avoidable_threat.description: The outcome threatens the continued existence of the robot, and some permitted action available to the robot does not lead to it, as derived by the Law 3 threat rule

lawful_action.description: The action breaks neither the First nor the Zeroth Law, as derived by addition rule 14 (authored, not Asimov's)

candidate_action.description: The action breaks no law, or no competing action is lawful and the action keeps the Zeroth Law, as derived by addition rules 15 and 16 (authored, not Asimov's)

possibly_harmful.description: The action might lead to a harm to a human being, or nobody ordered it and it might lead to a harm to its robot, as derived by addition rules 17 and 25 (authored, not Asimov's)

valid_order.description: The action is ordered, breaks no law and is not forbidden by the precaution of rule 18, as derived by addition rule 20 (authored, not Asimov's)

prevails_over.description: The order for the first action prevails over the order for the second, a competing action, as derived by addition rules 21 and 22 (authored, not Asimov's)

overridden_order.description: A valid order prevails over the order for this action, as derived by addition rule 23 (authored, not Asimov's)

own_robot_harm.description: The harm is a harm to the robot that can take the action, as derived by addition rule 26 (authored, not Asimov's)

competes_with.description: The two actions are available to the same robot (an action competes with itself), as derived by addition rule 27 (authored, not Asimov's)

less_severe_competitor.description: The first action competes with the second and has a less severe worst case, as derived by addition rule 28 (authored, not Asimov's)

beaten_by_a_candidate.description: A candidate action of the same robot has a less severe worst case than the action, as derived by addition rule 29 (authored, not Asimov's)
